label: prose:sm-params-higgs
title: Higgs sector (2)
html:
Parameter Framework status Anchor
m_H conjectural — T(2,8) torus-link identification; conditional Plancherel-trace ratio formula electroweak triplet
v (electroweak scale) open — competing conditional fixed-point and four-hop weak-jet scalings electroweak triplet

The Higgs mass has a conjectural identification: the Higgs is assigned the torus link T(2,8) within the electroweak triplet conjecture, alongside W = T(2,4) and Z = T(2,6). Because torus links have zero hyperbolic volume, their mass chain rests on two-strand Plancherel trace polynomials P_m(h) (h = q - q^{-1}) rather than hyperbolic volume. Dressing the W \to Z genus step by ([2]_q/2)^2 = 1 + h^2/4 reconciles the W- and Z-anchored mass ratios (m_Z/m_W within 175 parts per million of experiment) and places the (6/5)-scaled P_4(h_0)/P_2(h_0) scalar-to-gauge ratio near 125.1–125.5\;\mathrm{GeV} (corresponding to a positive tree-level Higgs quartic \lambda_H = m_H^2/(2v^2) \approx 0.129), whereas omitting the quantum-dimension dressing leaves a -0.66\% (124.37\;\mathrm{GeV}) residual under the Borromean 2G h_0^4 correction. Because neither the 6/5 prefactor nor the higher-order loop factor is derived from the category, the parameter remains conjectural.

The electroweak scale v remains open, with two distinct structural routes in tension. First, on the noncommutative Sweedler weak first jet, a four-hop charged-current contraction carries scaling (q_0^2 - 1)^8 \approx 8.41 \times 10^{-6} against G_F \mathfrak{m}_p^2 \approx 1.03 \times 10^{-5} (-18.1\%, or +10.5\% on v \approx 272.1\;\mathrm{GeV} under direct Frobenius-norm identification), whereas interpreting (q_0^2 - 1)^8 as a squared weak decay rate scales G_F \mathfrak{m}_p^2 as (q_0^2 - 1)^4 and underpredicts v by more than an order of magnitude at the proton scale (14.65\;\mathrm{GeV}). Second, the conditional Bring–Schwinger fixed-point cubic 1/\alpha_v = q([2]_q/2)[4]_q[6]_q[8]_q + 1/\pi - \alpha_v H(1 - \hbar_q^2\alpha_v) (H = [2]_q/(8\pi)) matches v/\mathfrak{m}_p to -29.4 parts per billion (and to +81.1 parts per billion without cubic iteration when the loop coupling is fixed to the parameter-free Sweedler factor 2^{1/4}(q_0^2 - 1)^4 < 1/30, avoiding the \alpha_2 > 1/30 incompatibility), yet rests on undischarged selections for the dressing exponent, the per-carrier zero-mode rule, and the \mathrm{SU}(2)_L loop sign. Because v normalises every Standard-Model mass via the Yukawa mechanism inside the G-action-on-substrate conjecture, reconciling this open electroweak scale with the calibrated volume–density and Hecke-energy mass chains remains an essential obligation.
